situation.margin_position: The 2025 operating margin of 0.4785 is falling from the 2022 peak of 0.6578. It is still above the company's long-run median of roughly 0.43 to 0.45, outside the loss years. Charter rates were high in 2024-2026 and were fixed in earlier, stronger markets, while depreciation and drydocking amortization are rising with the fleet.
situation.why: 2025 reflects a mostly contracted container fleet at 98.2% utilization, so earnings are stable, but the margin is still drifting down from the boom years. Many older charters at $40,000-58,000/day roll off in 2027-2028 and will reprice to market, and the 2026 drybulk spot rate surge adds some temporary upside. I treat the base year as representative of the near term but above the long-run level.

situation.why: 2025 revenue grew 2.8% and utilization was high, with no impairment or one-offs in operating income. Multi-year charters smooth revenue. The margin is drifting down as expiring charters reset and newbuilds on lower rates add depreciation, so I fade it toward the longer-run median rather than hold 2025. The drybulk spot segment adds cyclical upside and downside.

business_model.claim: Danaos Corporation owns container vessels and drybulk vessels, chartering containerships to liner companies and employing drybulk vessels on short-term time charters and voyage charters.
quotes: Danaos Corporation is an international owner of container vessels and drybulk vessels, chartering our container vessels to many of the world’s largest liner companies and employing our drybulk vessels on short-term time charters and voyage charters.

business_model.claim: Following its 2023 acquisition of drybulk vessels, Danaos operates in two reportable segments: a container vessels segment and a drybulk vessels segment.
quotes: Following the acquisition of the drybulk vessels in 2023, the Company operates in two separate segments in accordance with ASC 280: (i) a container vessels segment, as a provider of worldwide marine transportation services through time charter and bareboat charter arrangements; and (ii) a drybulk vessels segment, as a provider of drybulk commodity transportation services through time charter and voyage charter arrangements.

business_model.claim: As of February 25, 2026, the container segment deployed 75 containerships—73 on time charters and two on bareboat charters—to liner companies including CMA CGM, MSC, Hapag Lloyd, COSCO, PIL, Maersk, ONE, Sealead, OOCL, Samudera, Interasia Lines, Yang Ming, and ZIM.
quotes: As of February 25, 2026, 73 of the 75 containerships in our fleet were employed on time charters, of which two expire in 2026, and two containerships were employed on bareboat charters.
As of February 25, 2026, these customers included CMA CGM, MSC, Hapag Lloyd, COSCO, PIL, Maersk, ONE, Sealead, OOCL, Samudera, Interasia Lines, Yang Ming and ZIM.

business_model.claim: The drybulk segment employs 11 Capesize bulk carriers on short-term time charters and voyage charters in the spot market, serving 19 customers in 2025 and 14 customers in 2024.
quotes: We operate our drybulk carriers in the spot market, on short-term time charters and voyage charters.
As of February 25, 2026, on a fully delivered basis, our Capesize drybulk fleet will consist of 11 vessels with an aggregate capacity of 1,943,286 DWT.

Our drybulk carriers generated revenue from short-term time charter agreements and voyage charter agreements from 19 customers and 14 customers in the years ended December 31, 2025 and December 31, 2024, respectively.

business_model.claim: Consolidated operating revenues rose from $ 973,583 in 2023 to $ 1,014,110 in 2024 and $ 1,042,456 in 2025 (table in thousands).

Drybulk generated $46.6 million from voyage charters and $40.4 million from short-term time charters in 2025, and grew 57.3% year-over-year to $35.7 million out of $274.4 million total operating revenues in the three months ended June 30, 2026.
quotes: In 2025, we generated $46.6 million (2024: $47.0 million) of revenue from voyage charter agreements and $40.4 million (2024: $30.0 million) of revenue from short-term time charter agreements of our Capesize bulk carriers.
Operating revenues increased by $12.2 million, to $274.4 million in the three months ended June 30, 2026 from $262.2 million in the three months ended June 30, 2025.

Operating revenues of our drybulk vessels segment increased by 57.3%, or $13.0 million, to $35.7 million in the three months ended June 30, 2026, compared to $22.7 million of revenues in the three months ended June 30, 2025.

business_model.claim: Fleet size and vessel carrying capacity are the primary drivers of revenue, with 27 containerships and four Newcastlemax drybulk carriers under construction to expand the fleet.
quotes: The number of vessels in our fleet, and their TEU capacity for containerships or DWT capacity for drybulk vessels, is the primary factor in determining the level of our revenues.

As of February 25, 2026, we had a fleet of 75 containerships aggregating 477,491 TEUs, 27 under construction containerships aggregating 174,550 TEUs, 11 Capesize bulk carriers, including one scheduled to be delivered to us in March 2026, aggregating 1,943,286 DWT and four under construction Newcastlemax bulk carriers with an approximate aggregate capacity of 844,000 DWT.

business_model.claim: Charter rates and staggered multi-year contracts drive revenue stability, with $4.3 billion in contracted cash operating revenues over a 4.3 years weighted-average remaining container charter duration, though 21 containership charters expire in 2027.

As of February 25, 2026, the charters for two of our containerships are scheduled to expire in 2026 and 21 in 2027.

business_model.claim: Vessel operating and voyage costs are driven by fleet size, non-U.S. dollar crew wages, insurance premiums, and charter commissions of 1.03% to 2.5% to unaffiliated brokers, 2.0% to 5.0% to charterers, and 1.25% to Danaos Chartering or Danaos Shipping.

We also pay address commissions of 2.0% up to 5.0% to a limited number of our charterers.

In each of the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, we paid a fee to Danaos Chartering or Danaos Shipping, as applicable, of 1.25% on all freight, charter hire, ballast bonus and demurrage for each vessel.
